comment: Generated by runtime/http/go/stackconfig (cd runtime/http/go && go test ./stackconfig -run TestWriteParityVectors -update); do not edit. The Go, TypeScript and Rust HTTP runtimes each read every vector with their stackconfig readers (D51, D57, docs/stack-model.md sections 3.4 and 8.6). Per vector: reader is database (LoadDatabase, loadDatabase), service (LoadService, loadService), bucket (LoadBucket, loadBucket), memoryStore (LoadMemoryStore, loadMemoryStore, load_memory_store, D75), callers (LoadCallers, loadCallers) or cors (LoadCORS, loadCors, D55), and field the derived field's name. value is the ir derived value (an ir.DatabaseConnection, ir.ServiceEndpoint, ir.BucketConnection, ir.MemoryStoreConnection, ir.ServiceAuth or ir.CORSPolicy in its JSON form, which a refusal's may break), or null when no value encodes the vector's environment; variables are what ir.DerivedVariables makes of it. The environment the reader reads is variables with edits applied: a string sets the variable, even to the empty string, and null unsets it. want is the loaded value in the TypeScript runtime's shape ({url} or {cloudSql}; {url, credential?} with headers only when set; {name, endpoint?}; {store, url, auth, ca?, member?}, or null for a memory store none of whose variables is set, a disabled store; the serviceauth config the verifier takes, with members the environment leaves empty absent; {origins}, the origins in order with no repeat), null for a refusal. refusals lists the refusal's messages in order: the error's message joins them with newlines, and each line begins with its entry. workerOnly, when set, is the refusal of the Go and Rust readers, which refuse the members only a Worker reads (D64: a database's d1, a service's binding, a bucket's binding and r2), in place of want and refusals, which the TypeScript runtime's readers give.
